title: Diagonal orientation on a coordinate chart
statement:
Work in the finite-coefficient purity setting [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, uniformizer $\ell$, $n\geq1$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth, separated and of finite type, of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open subscheme and let $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ be an étale $Y$-morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Absolute separatedness of $Y$ is not assumed.

Use the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], the derived pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the coefficient twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Write $p_d:\mathbf A^d_Y\to Y$ and $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$ for each indicated smooth morphism $h$. Let $\vartheta_f:\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ be the diagonal orientation of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]: on separated target opens this is the composite $\beta_f\delta_f\alpha_f^{-1}$, where $\alpha_f:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_f$ is [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $\delta_f$ is the normalized section comparison [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and $\beta_f$ is the pullback to the zero section of vector-bundle purity [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity], for the normal bundle of the diagonal. The section invariant is [def-pur-section-invariant].

Then, under $Lj^*\omega_f\simeq\omega_{f|_U}$, the map $Lj^*\vartheta_f$ equals the coordinate-adjunction orientation
$$
\omega_{f|_U}=R(p_de)^!\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*\omega_{p_d}\xrightarrow{Le^*\vartheta^{\mathrm{aff}}_{p_d}}\Lambda_U(d)[2d].
$$
Here the first arrow uses composition of exceptional adjoints and the canonical étale identification $Re^!=Le^*$, and $\vartheta^{\mathrm{aff}}_{p_d}$ is the inverse of the comparison transposed from integration in the ordered affine coordinate tower, with the normalization specified in [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement].

proof.text: Domain and target localization. Cover $Y$ by affine opens $V$ and put $X_V=f^{-1}V$, $U_V=U\cap X_V$ and $A_V=\mathbf A^d_V$. These are the actual restrictions of $f,j,e$. Finite-type schemes over $k$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; their open subschemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Hence all these open inclusions are quasi-compact and finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. Finite type for their structure maps follows by composing finite sets of algebra generators on affine charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The affine $V$ is separated over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). Separatedness is preserved by base change [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] and composition [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e); thus $X_V,U_V,A_V$ and their fibre products used below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. The affine-space projection is smooth of dimension $d$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]; the other projections have dimension $d$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], and restricting their sources to the displayed opens preserves smoothness and the pointwise fibre dimension by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. We first compare the maps on $U_V$, writing $Y,X,U,A$ for these restricted schemes. The final step checks that this suffices without absolute separatedness of the original $Y$.

source.place: Before Step 1: domain of the diagonal and DNC construction on affine target opens

proof.text: The chart is separated. Put $h=f|_U=p_de$. The diagonal of $h$ is the pullback of the closed immersion $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_YX$ along $U\times_YU\to X\times_YX$, so $h$ is separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b); this makes explicit the relative separatedness inherited from $f$. The map $\Delta_e:U\to U\times_AU$ is the pullback of $\Delta_h:U\to U\times_YU$ along $U\times_AU\to U\times_YU$: the fibre-product equation says the two $U$-components coincide. Since $h$ is separated, $\Delta_h$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and its pullback is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Thus $e$ is separated by that same definition. This proves the separatedness used in the blueprint instead of assuming that an arbitrary étale map is separated. Also $U$ is quasi-compact and $A$ quasi-separated, so $e$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1); its local finite presentation, part of [def-weil-etale-morphism], makes it finite type.

source.place: Step 1: justification of the separated chart hypothesis

proof.text: Cartesian centres on a neighbourhood. Write $W=U\times_YU$, $W_0=A\times_YA$, and $q=e\times e:W\to W_0$. Each factor of $q$ is a base change of $e$, hence étale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; their composite is smooth of relative dimension $0+0=0$, hence étale, by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2), including its explicit dimension-zero étale case. The scheme-theoretic inverse image of $\Delta_A$ is $Z=U\times_AU$, a closed subscheme of $W$, since $\Delta_A$ is closed. The projection $Z\to U$ is the base change of $e$ along $e$, hence étale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] (Step 2), with section $\Delta_U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion], that section is open and closed in $Z$. Thus $Z\setminus\Delta_U(U)$ is closed in $W$, and its complement $W^\circ$ is an open neighbourhood of $\Delta_U$. On $W^\circ$ the inverse image of $\Delta_A$ is exactly $\Delta_U$ as a closed subscheme. The square of centres with top map $q^\circ:W^\circ\to W_0$ and base map $e:U\to A$ is therefore Cartesian. The restricted first projection $W^\circ\to U$ remains smooth of dimension $d$ and has closed section $\Delta_U$. All objects are separated finite type by Step 1.

source.place: Step 1: Cartesian square of centres, with the complementary closed subscheme removed

proof.text: Normal bundles in that square. Both diagonals are regular closed immersions of codimension $d$ by [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]; restricting the ambient scheme near the closed image does not change its conormal algebra, which lives on the closed image. Since the Cartesian ambient map $q^\circ$ is étale, it is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. By Step 3 the square with closed immersions $\Delta_U:U\hookrightarrow W^\circ$, $\Delta_A:A\hookrightarrow W_0$, ambient map $q^\circ$ and base map $e$ is a fibre product, so [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change] gives an isomorphism of graded $\mathcal O_U$-algebras $c:e^*\mathcal G_{\Delta_A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G_{\Delta_U}$ between the conormal algebras of [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], given on affine charts by $[a]\otimes r\mapsto[ar]$. Its degree-one part is the conormal isomorphism $e^*(\mathcal I_{\Delta_A}/\mathcal I_{\Delta_A}^2)\simeq\mathcal I_{\Delta_U}/\mathcal I_{\Delta_U}^2$ of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-flat-base-change], and its degree-zero part is the identity. Taking the relative spectra described in [def-pur-normal-bundle] gives $N_{\Delta_U/W}\simeq U\times_A N_{\Delta_A/W_0}$: the relative spectrum of $e^*\mathcal G_{\Delta_A}$ is the base change $U\times_A N_{\Delta_A/W_0}$ by the affine descriptions in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2), and $c$ gives the isomorphism by the anti-equivalence (3). The degree-zero augmentations correspond, so zero sections are preserved. Under [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion] this is $T_{U/Y}\simeq e^*T_{A/Y}$. It is the differential of $e$: a coordinate difference $x_i\otimes1-1\otimes x_i$ pulls back to the difference of its two pulled-back coordinates. Thus the normal map is the specific linear map induced by the Cartesian centres, not an arbitrarily chosen frame isomorphism.

source.place: Step 2: the induced normal map; Stacks Tags 0635 (divisors-lemma-conormal-algebra-functorial-flat) and 0473 (morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial-flat)

proof.text: Identify the source maps. The maps $p_d$ and $h$ are separated of finite type over the affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, target. Thus [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies the compactifiability required below; $\Lambda$ is finite. The canonical adjoint identification, including its normalization, is [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]: on ordinary étale derived categories $e^*p_d^{\times}K\simeq(p_de)^{\times}K$. The definition [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] transports these ordinary adjoints to the finite constructible pro-étale category. In that category, [lem-pur-co-smooth-etale-locality] says an étale map has trivial dualizing object. The tensor formula and composition compatibility of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](1),(4) therefore give $Re^!K\simeq Le^*K$ and $c_e:\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*\omega_{p_d}$. The same applies to open inclusions, including $W^\circ\hookrightarrow W$. Write $\alpha_h:C(p_{1,U},\Delta_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$ and $\alpha_p:C(p_{1,A},\Delta_A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_d}$ for [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. The étale comparison of section invariants, using $q^\circ\Delta_U=\Delta_A e$, gives a map $a:C(p_{1,U},\Delta_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*C(p_{1,A},\Delta_A)$. Here we restrict to $W^\circ$ first, using the preceding open comparison. One has $(Le^*\alpha_p)a=c_e\alpha_h$: both sides are the comparison for the same diagram: $p_{1,A}q^\circ=e p_{1,U}$, $p_{2,A}q^\circ=e p_{2,U}$, $q^\circ\Delta_U=\Delta_A e$, and $p_de=h$. More explicitly the base-change comparison in $\alpha$ is the counit mate in [def-pur-co-smoothness](3); paste it with the étale-composition square. The two pastings have this same composite, so [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1),(2),(4) identifies their mates, giving the displayed equality.

source.place: Step 3, first paragraph: exceptional composition, étale pullback, and the diagonal source comparison

proof.text: Compare the deformation arrows. Let $\delta_h$ and $\delta_p$ be the normalized DNC isomorphisms for these two diagonal sections. Factor the ambient map as $W^\circ\to U\times_Y A\to A\times_Y A$, with first map $(p_{1,U},e p_{2,U})$ and second map $(e,1)$. The first map is étale over the same base $U$, and the inverse image of the graph section $u\mapsto(u,e(u))$ is exactly $\Delta_U$. The graph pair is the base change along $e:U\to A$ of the affine diagonal pair. Apply the étale-localization compatibility of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] to the first map and its base-change compatibility to the second map. These applications stay in the separated finite-type domain checked in Step 1. They identify $\delta_h$ with $Le^*\delta_p$ under $a$ and the normal-bundle identification of Step 4. In formulas, if $b:C(\pi_U,z_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}Le^*C(\pi_A,z_A)$ denotes that normal comparison, then $b\delta_h=(Le^*\delta_p)a$. The normalization is essential: in the coordinates of [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](2),(4), the deformation coordinates are $u_i=x_i/t$, and both comparisons are the identity on the standard section invariant. Hence it is precisely the uniquely normalized comparison of the cited theorem that is identified, with no residual scalar. This uses the theorem's stated étale locality, rather than assuming that an arbitrary chosen deformation isomorphism is functorial.

source.place: Step 3, second paragraph: normalized DNC comparison under the Cartesian étale neighbourhood

proof.text: Compare the final arrows. Let $\beta_h:C(\pi_U,z_U)\to\Lambda_U(d)[2d]$ and $\beta_p:C(\pi_A,z_A)\to\Lambda_A(d)[2d]$ be the zero-section restrictions of vector-bundle purity. By the base-change and adjunction compatibility of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity], applied to the actual pullback bundle of Step 4, $\beta_h=(Le^*\beta_p)b$. The target identification is the canonical Tate pullback of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists]. This also respects the integration normalization: [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identifies the inverse vector-bundle comparison with the integration-transposed map on the ordinary étale site. In a linear trivialization, changing its frame preserves that actual trace by [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance]. Thus the identification in Step 4 does not change the orientation, and no determinant unit or sign is introduced.

source.place: Step 4, first sentence: vector-bundle integration and the linear normal identification

proof.text:
Multiply the three identities. By the specified diagonal construction, $\vartheta_h=\beta_h\delta_h\alpha_h^{-1}$. Steps 5--7 give
$$
\vartheta_h=(Le^*\beta_p)b\delta_h\alpha_h^{-1}=(Le^*\beta_p)(Le^*\delta_p)a\alpha_h^{-1}=(Le^*(\beta_p\delta_p\alpha_p^{-1}))c_e=(Le^*\vartheta_{p_d})c_e.
$$
For the vector bundle $p_d:A\to Y$, [det-sp-orientation-vector-bundle] identifies $\vartheta_{p_d}$ with its vector-bundle orientation. The coordinate normalization in [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement], at $K=\Lambda_Y$, identifies the same diagonal composite with the inverse of the ordered coordinate-adjunction comparison. Consequently $\vartheta_{p_d}=\vartheta^{\mathrm{aff}}_{p_d}$, giving the required equality on $U_V$. This is equality of the displayed morphisms, since the first two equalities use the identities $b\delta_h=(Le^*\delta_p)a$ and $(Le^*\alpha_p)a=c_e\alpha_h$, not just isomorphism of their sources and targets.

source.place: Step 4: combining the three canonical factors and identifying the affine-space normalization

proof.text: Return to the original target. For $U_V\hookrightarrow U$ and $X_V\hookrightarrow X$, the diagonal pairs are the base changes along these open inclusions, after restricting their ambient schemes near the sections. The smooth source comparison restricts by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](3),(4), the normalized deformation comparison restricts by [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and the vector-bundle arrow restricts by [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. Tate targets restrict by [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists]. Therefore the orientations defined by these three factors on the separated target opens are the restrictions of $\vartheta_f$ and of its open restriction to $U$, while the coordinate-adjunction map restricts to the coordinate-adjunction map for $e|_{U_V}$; for this last assertion use the actual base-change equality $t_{p_d,V}\operatorname{Ex}_!=v^*t_{p_d,Y}$ in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], transport it by [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], and take the counit mates using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Each open target and the original target is Noetherian, as checked in Step 1, so the trace statement applies. To justify detection of equality, compose each of the two candidate maps $Lj^*\omega_f\to\Lambda_U(d)[2d]$ with $(Lj^*\vartheta_f)^{-1}$, and shift by $-2d$. The resulting maps are endomorphisms of the sheaf $\Lambda_U(d)$ in degree zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] these are ordinary sheaf maps. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], these restrictions are the ordinary restrictions to the localized pro-étale sites, with the same constant coefficient ring. They agree on the open cover $\{U_V\}$ by Step 8; the uniqueness assertion of [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] makes them equal globally. Composing back proves the claimed equality. If $U$ is empty, the sheaf category has only zero objects and the conclusion is immediate. For $d=0$, normal bundles have rank zero, the standard DNC comparison is the identity, and the coordinate trace is the identity adjunction, as explicitly covered by [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement].

source.place: Open restriction, equality on arbitrary target opens, and rank-zero/empty cases
